summary: Phase 1 hardens four trust primitives first—execution identity, legacy control-path auth, runtime isolation, and rollback integrity—then uses those primitives to secure websocket task visibility and make final task outcomes plus metrics reflect actual preview readiness and recovery state.
approach: Use three waves. Wave 1 fixes independent high-risk seams without rewriting the product. Wave 2 authenticates websocket log access and propagates richer task status to the UI. Wave 3 makes develop/deploy terminal outcomes and monitoring truthful by combining persisted execution identity, rollback checkpoints, and preview-readiness verification.

stages: Task creation -> Celery enqueue -> worker execution -> status/log publish -> websocket/UI consumption
Snapshot creation -> archive integrity metadata -> staged rollback -> preview restart/validation
Legacy and websocket access -> authenticated ownership checks -> sanitized responses/events
Truthful terminal outcome -> Prometheus metrics -> /metrics and stats consumers

design_decisions: Keep the modular monolith and tighten internal boundaries instead of extracting services.
Preserve route compatibility where possible, but require auth and stop returning secrets on risky legacy routes.
Reuse existing task_service, version_service, websocket_service, and metrics seams instead of introducing new frameworks.

patterns: backend/api/v2/tasks.py uses get_current_user/require_role for authenticated task APIs.
backend/tasks/_helpers.py provides fresh AsyncSession lifecycle for Celery workers.
backend/tests/conftest.py provides async client/auth fixtures and resets Prometheus registry.
conventions: Backend changes should stay inside api -> services -> models/core/utils boundaries.
Add targeted pytest coverage in backend/tests/ near the touched behavior.
Keep user-facing status semantics explicit and machine-verifiable.
dependencies: Redis pub/sub for websocket log fan-out.
Celery worker tasks for develop/deploy/test execution.
Site runtime restart path in backend/services/site_service.py.
Prometheus metrics exposure via backend/core/metrics.py and backend/main.py.
